title: What Is a Resume and What Is Its Purpose?
excerpt: A simple explanation of what a resume is, why it exists, and why one resume does not fit every purpose.

blocks.text: What Is a Resume and What Is Its Purpose?

Let me explain it very simply and in plain language: a resume is your showcase for introducing yourself. You need to introduce yourself and show the work you have done, or in other words, prove that you have worked in your field and have expertise. The tool that does this job is the resume.
If I want to define it in one line:
A resume is a tool for introducing yourself for a specific work or academic position or anything else.
Right here a point comes up that is seen as the most basic flaw in resumes:
The argument that is made is that since a resume means showing I have expertise and work experience and so on, I will write everyyyy single thing I have ever done in it. The more I write, the better!
I will explain more about this in other notes.
A Different Resume for Every Purpose
And the last point I should explain in this note:

A specific resume must be written for every specific thing --> if it's for continuing studies and PhD, it should be an academic resume, if it's for work, it should be a work resume, and these have fundamental differences with each other.
But here and in this folder, as its name makes clear, we will only talk about the academic resume.
